significance.justification: Verified true, the conclusion would be that a language-localized circuit is causally reused across arithmetic, logic, bracket, and code reasoning, with a measurable "depth-by-ablation interaction" in which disrupting it increasingly harms performance as structural nesting deepens; this is both a form-(iii) scaling relation and a form-(ii) cross-domain causal mechanism. It establishes a behavioral phenomenon across four task families and a mechanistic explanation involving the "rank-ordered component set S_syn," thereby predicting depth-dependent intervention effects beyond any single benchmark rather than merely showing that syntax is represented. The negative branch is also informative and determinate: conditional on finding a localizable S_syn, a flat non-linguistic depth effect would support the explicitly distinguished state that "the structure engine is domain-specific," bearing directly on the language-versus-thought decomposition discussed by Mahowald et al. (2024, Trends in Cognitive Sciences). In the topic-substitution self-check, the generic question of how language relates to intelligence would not earn this score; the extra weight comes specifically from the proposed cross-domain depth law and shared causal substrate.

reach.justification: The reusable handles are the "rank-ordered component set S_syn," its "depth-by-ablation interaction coefficient," and the resulting intervention that lets practitioners "probe or steer reasoning via the shared syntax circuit." Steering can act before or during an answer and thus provides some lead time, while the ablation slope is also a post-hoc diagnostic; after S_syn is re-extracted in another model, the substantive prediction remains that sensitivity should increase with nesting depth across structurally distinct tasks, so more than a search procedure transfers. Scope is meaningful across numeric, logical, bracketed, and code tasks and several transformer models, but the claim explicitly limits itself to "open-weight 7-8B models as a mechanistic case study" and leaves frontier-model generalization open; likely downstream users are interpretability researchers and model auditors rather than researchers outside AI. The topic-substitution check lowers no further: language–intelligence research alone supplies neither this circuit handle nor the transferable depth relation, although the restricted model scope prevents top-band reach.
